title: G class (v11 G1-G10): the P14 line-identity comparator resolved name collisions from the expected ledger and its gates were incomplete
what_went_wrong: EQUAL-CTX picked the actual code from the expected ledger (circular): a wrong code present in the ledger passed.

--expect MATCH ignored payment equality and the predicted form/ledger models; duplicate ledger keys were overwritten; an empty visit list passed 0/0; NULL numerics became 0; quantity was not compared for every component; fresh-B had no time boundary; P12 reconcile printed coverage without asserting it.
root_cause: The comparator was designed to prove the shapes the fixture exercised; the acceptance predicate was not required to be false for a plant that kept the same name and price.
detection: Astra v11 (66/100) finding G1-G10, each verified against the source in the P15 task doc section 1.
impact: The 300-visit clean result of P14 rested on a comparator that could not fail the C2 plant (shown on the same scratch copy in P15).

correction.applied: P15: p15_line_identity.py (source-row identity, EQUAL-SRC, stricter --expect, input errors exit 2, fresh-B INSERT by benchmark@ at/after the run start), p13_sample_compare.py B4/B5, p12 reconcile B6; P16 closed the residual fresh-B window and NULL-payment gaps.
correction.result: P15 C4: fixture 27/27, real 300/300, 0 line differences; P16 rerun under the stricter rule: see R5 section 28

rule: An acceptance predicate is not accepted until a plant that differs only in the property it claims to check makes it fail, on the old bytes it passes.
